title: Normalize GPU build matrix and runtime kernel fallback for CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS transitions
creator: Asha Patel
description: We have drift across our GPU build and runtime surfaces: multiple Docker images and build flags target mixed CUDA 12/13 toolchains, Triton plugin ABI changes (v2/v3), and multiple CUTLASS forks. This ticket standardizes the build matrix, introduces a small runtime compatibility shim to detect unavailable optimized kernels and fall back to a safe reference path, and adds CI/benchmark coverage to catch regressions early. Goals: 1) make developers able to build a single wheel/image that supports both CUDA12 and CUDA13 target hosts where possible, 2) ensure the serving runtime can gracefully degrade to a slower but correct kernel when a newer CUTLASS/Triton symbol is not present, 3) add CI smoke tests and perf thresholds to avoid silent regressions when we bump deps.
tasks: Inventory current Docker images, wheels, and build flags across repos (serving, compiler, ops). Link artifact list in Confluence.
Define canonical build matrix: primary images for cuda12-cudnn8, cuda13-cudnn9, and a fallback cpu image. Document expected symbol sets for each.
Add CMake/meson guards to selectively enable CUTLASS extensions and build alternative kernels when symbols are missing.
Implement lightweight runtime kernel probe: on init, attempt dlsym/RTLD_NEXT lookup for critical Triton/CUTLASS entrypoints and record availability flags.
Implement fallback code path: when an optimized kernel is flagged missing, route to a reference kernel implementation (not the slow Python path) and emit a telemetry metric.
Add canary CI matrix entries (short runs) for CUDA12/CUDA13 with Triton v2 and v3; include a perf microbenchmark job that runs a fixed prompt set and checks p50 latency within threshold.
Create perf/regression dashboard and alert rule: perf drop >10% or error-rate increase >1% triggers PagerDuty to infra team.
Update packaging to tag images with supported ABI sets and add clear release notes for runtime-1.22.
Run integration tests against Dedicated pool machines and one Private deployment image to validate behavior under real hardware.
Migrate a subset of traffic via runtime rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions.
Post-mortem and follow-ups: capture any edge-case kernels that require backport patches to CUTLASS/Triton or custom wrappers.
acceptance_criteria: A single documented build matrix exists and is checked into the runtime repo docs directory.
Serving runtime emits a metric 'gpu.optimized_kernel_available' per kernel name and exposes fallback count 'gpu.kernel_fallback_count' to the console.
CI matrix runs for cuda12 and cuda13 pass on short smoke tests and the perf microbenchmark p50 latency is within the agreed threshold (<= 10% degradation vs baseline).
Images/wheels are tagged with explicit ABI support metadata and publish step fails if tags are inconsistent.
Rollout executed to 25% without customer-facing errors and dashboards show no regression alerts for 72 hours.
Related follow-up tickets created for any kernels that need upstream fixes with clear owners.
